research:
I've gathered enough to answer. My web fetches were refused by the proxy, so I couldn't open Yahoo Finance or any article directly. Everything below comes from search-result snippets. I left out every result dated after 2026-08-22.

## 1. Resolution source
- **What decides it:** Yahoo Finance BZ=F, [history page](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BZ=F/history/). The fetch was refused, so I could not read the latest close there myself.
- **Weekend rule applies:** 2026-09-19 is a Saturday, so the question resolves on the Friday 2026-09-18 close.
- **Contract roll:** BZ=F follows the front-month ICE Brent contract. By standard ICE rules, which I did not confirm for 2026, the October 2026 contract expires around 2026-08-31. On 2026-09-18, BZ=F should therefore be the November 2026 contract. Any gap between the October and November prices (likely backwardation in a tight market) will show up as a jump in the series at the roll.
- **Latest close:**
  - 2026-08-21: Brent futures closed up 61 cents at **$94.39**. Oil finished the week more than 5% higher. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/21/oil-prices-us-iran.html)
  - The $94.39 figure comes from a search summary. The article it came from may not name the session, so check it against Yahoo.
  - Barchart's October Brent page showed a one-month high of 94.83 on 08/21/26. [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CBV26)
- 2026-08-20: Brent rose 2.4% to close at $93.78. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/20/oil-prices-brent-wti-hormuz-trump.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The market is highly volatile and driven by the US-Iran war and the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-22: Iran criticized the coming US sanctions as "extraterritorial sovereignty." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/22/iran-criticizes-us-sanctions-extraterritorial-sovereignty.html)
- 2026-08-21: Prices were little changed after Iran's president said Tehran wants the war to end soon. WTI was about $87.06. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/21/oil-prices-us-iran.html)
- 2026-08-20: Oil rose after Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US would impose the "toughest sanctions in history" and collapse Iran with economic pressure. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/20/oil-prices-brent-wti-hormuz-trump.html)
- 2026-08-17: Brent settled at $90.87, up 2.7%, after the US and Iran let a June memorandum of understanding expire. Iran threatened to escalate in Hormuz. Rapidan's Bob McNally expects Brent to head back toward $100 as Chinese imports rise. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/oil-prices-iran-war-strait-hormuz.html)
- **Hormuz flows (around 2026-08-17):** Estimates disagree.
  - US Energy Secretary Wright says about 9 mb/d is moving through the strait.
  - Commodity Context puts the peak nearer 7 mb/d.
  - The pre-war level was about 20 mb/d.
  - [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz.html)
- 2026-08-12: Prices rose as attacks dented hopes that Hormuz would reopen. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/12/oil-prices-rise-as-attacks-dent-hopes-for-strait-of-hormuz-reopening)
- **Early August (Trading Economics item dated 2026-08-04):** Brent was just above $79 and down about 10% on the week. The drop came on hopes for an interim Hormuz deal. Qatar said a proposal was ready, and Trump called off planned military action. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil/news/572709)
- 2026-07-31: Brent settled at $90.12, its strongest month since March. [EnergyNow](https://energynow.com/2026/08/oil-price-rises-after-iran-says-it-stops-ships-in-hormuz/)

## 4. Base rates and volatility
- **Recent path:** about $90 (July 31), then about $79 (early August), then $90.87 (Aug 17), then about $94.4 (Aug 21). That is roughly a 19% swing within three weeks.
- **Earlier 2026 swings:**
  - April 2026: Brent fell 12.7% in one week to $95.20 on a two-week ceasefire. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/energy/oil/brent-falls-below-100-on-2-week-us-iran-ceasefire-deal/56226)
  - Mid-June 2026: Brent fell about 8% in one week as Hormuz exports restarted. [PGJ](https://pgjonline.com/news/2026/june/brent-set-for-8-weekly-fall-as-hormuz-exports-restart)
- **What that implies for four weeks:** In this regime, weekly moves of 5 to 13% are common. Over about four weeks, a one-standard-deviation band of roughly ±12 to 15% (about ±$11 to 14 from $94) looks consistent with recent history. This is my rough estimate, not a computed figure.
- **Roll effect:** The October-to-November spread could shift BZ=F by a few dollars at the end of August. I could not find the spread itself.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Reuters August poll:** analysts' average 2026 Brent forecast was about $85.08. This figure comes from a search summary, and I did not see the article. [OilPrice](https://oilprice.com/Energy/Oil-Prices/Oil-Price-Forecasts-Jump-as-Hormuz-Disruption-Drags-On.html)
- Rapidan (2026-08-17) sees a move back toward $100.
- **Prediction markets:** Kalshi runs daily and weekly Brent markets (KXBRENTD, KXBRENTW), including one for the week ending 2026-09-18. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxbrentw/brent-oil/kxbrentw-26sep1817) I could not find pricing from on or before 2026-08-22, and I found no Polymarket or Manifold market.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2026-09-18
- **US sanctions:** A sweeping sanctions package on Iran is expected. Bessent promised an "economic D-Day" in an op-ed dated 2026-08-23, which is just after the cutoff. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/22/iran-criticizes-us-sanctions-extraterritorial-sovereignty.html)
- **US-Iran talks:** The interim deal has lapsed. Either an interim Hormuz agreement or escalation is the main two-way risk.
- **Contract roll:** The October Brent contract expires around 2026-08-31, and BZ=F switches to November.
- **OPEC+:** The monthly meeting of the eight-country group, usually held in early September. I could not confirm a date.
- **Monthly reports:**
  - EIA STEO, around 2026-09-09
  - OPEC MOMR and IEA OMR, around 2026-09-10 to 09-11
  - Weekly EIA inventory data
- **Fed:** The FOMC decision is around 2026-09-16.
- **Weather:** The Atlantic hurricane season is at its peak.
